Definition: to cleave; generally, to rend, break, rip or open
BiblicalUsage: Baqa means to split open, to cleave, to break through. The fountains of the great deep are broken up when the flood comes, Moses lifts his rod and the sea is divided, Isaiah says waters will break out in the wilderness, and Zechariah says the Mount of Olives will cleave in the middle on the day of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word belongs to God alone in the end, because only He splits seas and mountains. Men break ground with ploughs, but God breaks open the deep, and I hold that the same hand that opened the sea for Israel will open the mountain for her return.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea; Noah and the Flood
